text.p: Pilots of Algerian state-owned airline Air Algerie on Tuesday staged a strike for a second day strike bringing traffic at Algiers airport to a near standstill, officials said.
"Yes, the strike goes on the same as yesterday (Monday)," said an Algiers airport spokeswoman speaking by telephone from the Algerian capital.

Air Algerie carries more than three million passengers a year, serving particularly North Africa, France and other European destinations, and a wide domestic network. But the airline has faced repeated financial problems and brief strikes by pilots, most of whom are union members.
The Algerian newspaper L'Authentique said on Tuesday "Algiers airport was paralysed by the (pilots) wildcat strike".
Algerian state-run radio called the strike a "surprise" and said the company was expecting traffic to return to normal later on Tuesday.

The pilots, at the call of the main airline union Syndicat des Pilotes des Lignes Algeriennes, walked out in solidarity with colleagues, who were on a hunger strike to protest against the dismissal of 52 pilots after a previous strike over pay.

Union officials have been on hunger strike since last week to protest at the lay-off of unionised pilots who rejected Air Algerie's order last June to resume duties during a strike. The pilots had then staged the strike to press for higher wages and better working conditions.
But Air Algerie's director general Faisal Khalil said last July his company's dire financial situation did not enable it to meet all the pay claims of the pilots.
